moat_against: Commodity containerboard/corrugated product — pricing follows published indices, customers can dual-source from Smurfit Westrock, Packaging Corp and regional mills
Gross margin stuck at 28.0-29.6% over the last five fiscal years (fundamentals.json) — no pricing-power expansion through a cycle
DS Smith EMEA business took a ~$2.5B goodwill impairment within a year of acquisition and is now reported to be saleable for under $6B vs ~$9.9B paid — the acquired franchise destroyed value
Low/negative returns on capital in the filed history: FY2025 net loss $3.516B, TTM net income -$3.438B (fundamentals.json); operating-income history is thin against a ~$38B asset base
Cyclical end demand (e-commerce, food/beverage, industrial) plus OCC/energy/transport cost exposure management cannot pass through reliably
moat_for: Largest North American containerboard/corrugated packaging scale — mill and box-plant network density lowers delivered cost and service lead times regionally
Integrated recycled-fiber collection and mill system — a real, if modest, input-cost and supply-security advantage
Long-standing relationships with large national food, beverage and e-commerce shippers; multi-plant supply agreements are sticky at the contract level, if not the price level
moat_justification: Scale and network density in North American containerboard/corrugated packaging plus integrated recycled fiber give a narrow cost advantage, but the product is a commodity priced off indices, gross margin has stayed at 28.0-29.6% for five years, returns on capital are low to negative (FY2025 net loss $3,516M on the DS Smith goodwill impairment), and the EMEA acquisition destroyed value within a year — no durable pricing power. Moat 3/10.
name: International Paper Company
one_liner: Commodity packaging, moat 3/10 — does not clear 15% on any defensible base: 4.6% weighted IRR on the current-perimeter TTM base (IV@15% $5.84 vs $34.05 price); it clears 15% only below ~$5.84 on TTM numbers and below ~$13.18 even on the flattering pre-deal median base.
